name: emit_formatted_string
description: Walks a format string, passing literal bytes to a character-output callback and expanding each percent conversion. It parses flag, width, precision and length modifiers, handles character, string, octal, unsigned and base-16 conversions, and recurses for nested numeric output, returning the count of characters written or a failure value if the callback fails.

name: perform_signed_division
description: Records whether the two signed input registers have opposite signs, calls another routine to do the division, and negates that result when the signs differed. It returns the quotient in the high word of a 64-bit value paired with the second input.

name: negate_result_if_negative
description: Calls another routine, then negates the value it returns when the first input was negative. The result is returned together with the second input in a 64-bit value.

name: call_and_return_concatenated
description: Calls another routine and returns a 64-bit value built from the original second input and the value the call leaves in its result register. It does no other work.

name: call_self_recursively
description: Calls itself and then returns, with no other work, so it would recurse without end if reached. The routine has a single caller.

name: perform_32bit_division
description: Divides a 32-bit dividend by a 32-bit divisor. When the divisor's high half is nonzero it runs a 16-step shift-and-subtract loop; otherwise it uses 16-bit divide operations, and it returns the quotient and remainder packed into one 64-bit value.

name: compute_string_length
description: Walks a zero-terminated byte string from the given pointer until it reaches the terminating zero, then returns the number of bytes before that terminator. It does not modify memory.

name: call_routine_and_return
description: Calls one other routine and returns without changing any data itself. It is reached through an address reference and from one caller.

name: invoke_three_helper_routines
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code is available. The facts show 21 instructions that call three other routines and are reached from two callers, one of them through an address reference; the purpose cannot be determined from this evidence.

name: stub_return_immediately
description: The decompiled body contains only a return with no work, so the routine does nothing when called. It is reached through an address reference from one caller.

name: call_two_helper_routines
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code is available. The facts show 15 instructions that call two other routines and are reached from two callers, including one address reference; the purpose cannot be determined from this evidence.

name: store_byte_advance_pointer
description: Reads one byte from a fixed offset of a base register, writes it to the location held in a pointer register, and advances that pointer by one. It returns the byte that was written.

name: call_routine_across_range
description: Steps from a computed start address to a computed end address in fixed steps of 22 bytes, calling another routine with each position. The bounds are offsets from the address register, and the routine is reached through an address reference from one caller.

name: reset_buffer_descriptor_state
description: Returns a failure value when given no descriptor. Otherwise, if the descriptor's state byte is set, it calls helper routines chosen by the state bits, then clears the descriptor's pointer, count and state fields and returns a combined status.

name: reset_buffer_descriptor_inline
description: Performs the same reset as its sibling routine but reads the descriptor directly from the address register instead of an argument. It calls helper routines selected by the descriptor's state bits, then clears the pointer, count and state fields and returns a combined status.

name: write_byte_to_buffer
description: Stores a handler routine in a global slot, then writes one byte into a buffer descriptor and returns it. It returns a failure value once an error flag is set, requests storage through a helper when the buffer has none, and sends single-byte buffers through a helper call.

name: write_byte_to_buffer_inline
description: Writes one byte from a frame offset into a buffer descriptor and returns it, using the same error-flag and storage-allocation checks as its sibling. Buffers with a size of one are written through a helper call, and larger buffers are written directly with the position advanced.

name: write_byte_or_clear_buffer
description: Clears the buffer descriptor and returns zero when its size field is -1. Otherwise it allocates storage through a helper if none exists, then stores one byte, using a helper call for single-byte buffers and direct writes for larger ones.

name: write_byte_through_buffer
description: Stores one byte from a frame offset into a buffer descriptor, first requesting storage through a helper when none exists. Single-byte buffers go through a helper call that sets an error flag on failure, and larger buffers receive the byte directly; the routine returns the byte or a failure value.

name: write_byte_advance_position
description: Writes one byte from a frame offset into a buffer, advances the buffer position, and returns a value packing the end offset with the byte. It performs no error checking and makes one helper call.

name: find_free_table_entry
description: Scans a table of 22-byte records from a computed base and returns the first record whose flag byte is zero, after clearing its three leading words. It returns a null pointer when every record is in use.

name: claim_free_entry_from_position
description: Searches forward from the current record pointer through 22-byte records for one whose flag byte is zero, clears its three leading words and returns it. It returns a null pointer when the scan reaches the end of the table.

name: clear_record_header_words
description: Zeroes the first two longwords and the third longword of the record referenced by the address register. It returns nothing.

name: initialize_buffer_record
description: Initializes a buffer record passed by pointer. If a helper returns no storage, it sets the size to one and points the buffer into the record itself; otherwise it sets the size to 1024, marks the record as allocated, stores the storage pointer, and sets a flag when a second helper returns nonzero.

name: setup_buffer_record_direct
description: Sets a record's buffer size to 1024 and marks it as allocated, then stores a pointer read from a global slot into the record's buffer field. It sets a flag in the record when a helper returns nonzero.

name: release_all_list_nodes
description: Walks a singly linked list whose head is held in a global slot, calling a helper with each node and its stored size plus eight. It then clears the head slot and returns zero.

name: release_all_list_nodes_inline
description: Repeats the list-release loop starting from the node in the address register, calling a helper with each node and its stored size plus eight. It then clears the global head slot and returns zero.

name: allocate_and_link_node
description: Stores a handler routine in a global slot, then allocates a node of the requested size through a helper. On success it links the node at the front of a global list, records the caller's pointer in it, and returns the usable area after the node header, or null on failure.

name: push_node_onto_list
description: Pushes a node onto the front of a global list, storing the previous head as the node's link and the caller's pointer in its second field. It returns the usable area after the node header.

name: forward_low_word_argument
description: Forwards the low 16 bits of its argument to another routine and then returns. It performs no other operations.

name: remove_node_from_list
description: Searches a global linked list for the node whose data area matches the argument, unlinks it when found, and passes it to a helper with its stored size plus eight before returning zero. It returns a failure value when no node matches.

name: remove_node_from_list_inline
description: Searches the global list for the node matching the record in the address register, unlinks it, releases it through a helper using its size plus eight, and returns zero. It returns a failure value when no node is found.

name: unlink_node_from_list
description: Removes a node from a global linked list by pointing its predecessor, or the list head, at the node's successor. It then makes one helper call and returns zero.

name: pop_list_head_node
description: Sets the head of a global list to the successor of the node in the address register, makes one helper call, and returns zero.

name: invoke_table_entry_handler
description: Validates a 16-bit index against a stored table count and checks that the table entry at that index is set. An invalid index records an error code and returns the failure value; otherwise it calls the handler stored in the entry and returns one if the handler reports nonzero, zero otherwise.

name: test_table_entry_interactive
description: Looks up the table entry at the index stored in the frame and passes its value to a helper that wraps the DOS IsInteractive call. It returns true when that check is nonzero.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Returns zero unconditionally and does no other work. It is reached through an address reference from one caller.

name: delete_file_record_error
description: Calls a helper that wraps the DOS DeleteFile function. When that call fails, it reads the error code through a helper that wraps the DOS IoErr function, stores it in a global slot and returns minus one; on success it returns zero.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Returns zero unconditionally and does no other work. It is reached through an address reference from one caller.

name: transfer_record_if_mode_set
description: Returns minus one and records error code five when the record's low two mode bits are zero. Otherwise it calls a helper with the record's pointer, a stored value and a stored size, and when that helper returns minus one it records the error code from a DOS IoErr wrapper and returns minus one.

name: write_record_or_store_error
description: Calls a helper with a record pointer and two stored arguments. When the helper returns minus one, it stores the error code from a DOS IoErr wrapper in a global slot and returns minus one; otherwise it returns the helper's value.

name: stub_return_immediately
description: Contains only a return and does nothing when called. It is reached through an address reference from one caller.

name: check_signal_mask_bit
description: Calls a helper with zero and a mask value, then tests the returned bits against that mask. When the bit is set and a stored value is zero it returns the bits; when it is set and the stored value is nonzero it calls a second helper; otherwise it returns zero.

name: call_and_return_zero
description: Calls one other routine, ignores its result and returns zero. It is reached through an address reference from one caller.

name: write_fixed_string_output
description: Passes a constant address and the length four to a helper, forwards the returned value to a DOS Write wrapper, then calls a routine through a pointer stored in the global data table. It returns nothing.

name: run_optional_handler_then_call
description: Calls the handler stored in a global slot when that slot is set, then calls another routine and returns. It is reached through a pointer in the data section.

name: release_all_global_resources
description: Works through the global resources in turn: it calls a helper for each entry of a counted table and then for the table itself, runs an optional handler, and calls a helper on each stored pointer that is set. It returns the value saved in the stack frame.

name: release_global_resources_with_supervisor
description: Performs the same global sequence as its counterpart: a helper for each table entry and for the table itself, followed by the optional handler and helper calls on the stored pointers that are set. When a state bit is set it makes an Exec Supervisor library call around the handler.

name: release_paired_buffers
description: When a stored primary pointer is unset, it calls a helper with a second stored pointer and a size scaled by four, provided that pointer is set. Otherwise it calls one helper with the primary pointer and a second helper with a different stored pointer, then returns the value saved in the stack frame.

name: call_helper_then_release_pointer
description: Calls one helper, then passes a stored pointer to a second helper, and returns the value saved in the stack frame.

name: release_table_entry_by_index
description: Validates a 16-bit index against the stored table count and checks that the entry is in use. An invalid index records error code two and returns minus one; otherwise, unless the entry's high flag bit is set, it calls a helper with the stored value, clears the entry and returns zero.

name: close_handle_and_clear
description: Calls the DOS Close wrapper on the handle stored at the argument when the high flag bit of its flag word is clear, then clears the stored handle and returns zero.

On success it fills the block's type, status and pointer fields from the frame, calls a helper, and passes the block or the block's offset-twenty field to a second helper depending on a frame value.

name: initialize_record_from_frame
description: Fills an existing record's type, status and pointer fields from the caller's frame, then calls a helper. It passes the record's offset-twenty field or the record itself to a second helper, depending on a frame value, and returns nothing.

description: Allocates a buffer through a library call and, when that succeeds, disables interrupts, runs timed wait loops, and writes the disk controller's data pointer, sync word and mode registers. It then calls library routines to finish and returns nothing; it does nothing when the allocation fails.

name: run_numbered_picture_loop
description: Program entry point: copies a text argument into a global name buffer of up to 51 characters and appends the literal text 00.pic. It opens the libraries it needs, allocates a signal, and loops waiting on that signal while advancing the two-digit number in the file name; it returns twenty when the library setup fails.

name: signal_task_if_flags_clear
description: Signals a task through the library's Signal entry when two flag bits in a global word are both clear, then returns zero. The facts list the joystick and mouse button registers as touched, but the pseudo-code only tests the global flags.

name: write_packed_iff_picture_body
description: Converts a block of 32 16-bit words into bytes, run-length encodes the result with PackBits-style count bytes, and writes it to an open file as an IFF FORM with a BODY chunk. It allocates its output buffer through a library call and closes the file through a DOS wrapper.

name: boot_allocate_and_launch_block
description: Allocates memory through a library call and returns two if that fails. It records the block, fills in fields of a request structure and makes a second library call; on success it passes control to a routine at a fixed offset inside the allocated block and returns its value, otherwise it returns three.

name: open_dos_library_check
description: Records two global base values, runs a helper and returns four if it fails, then calls another helper and makes a library call at minus 210 when a structure field is zero. It finishes with a library call at minus 96, returning zero on success and one on failure; the referenced text names the DOS library.

name: start_copper_list_display
description: Opens the graphics library through a library call and returns one on failure. On success it writes the copper list pointer, starts the copper through its jump register, enables DMA through the DMA control register, makes further library calls for interrupt setup, and returns zero.

name: unpack_packbits_stream
description: Decodes a PackBits-style run-length stream into a buffer until a remaining-length counter reaches zero. A non-negative control byte copies that many plus one literal bytes, and a negative one repeats the following byte; a negative remaining count returns four.

name: unpack_packbits_stream_variant
description: Decodes a PackBits-style stream from a source pointer into a destination pointer while counting down a total length. Negative control bytes repeat the next byte and other control bytes copy literal runs, returning zero when the length is consumed and four when the counter goes negative.

name: rotate_eight_byte_entry_fields
description: Writes the DMA control register value and decrements a frame counter. When the counter reaches zero it resets it to three and shifts the word field of each eight-byte table entry back by one slot, storing the saved first value in the last entry.

It copies and transforms stream bytes into block fields, calls a helper for each block, sets flag bits in a lookup table, and increments a global counter when a condition holds, stopping when its remaining count reaches minus one.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:07C8
name: copy_flagged_block_bytes
description: Calls a helper, then if the byte at offset 22 of the source block is non-negative, copies the bytes at offsets 22, 23, 24 and 26 into word fields of a second structure. It sets the source bytes at offsets 22 and 23 to 255 as it does so.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:07FE
name: copy_table_to_fixed_buffer
description: Copies fourteen 32-bit values from a source table whose base address is computed from a global index into a fixed destination buffer. It updates the global pointer to the source position during the copy.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0838
name: init_two_records_and_idle
description: Calls a helper, clears and sets global words, then initialises two records with constant fields and a flag bit each, calling a helper for each. It ends in an endless loop.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:088C
name: init_single_record_then_idle
description: Writes constant global words and fixed record fields, then calls a helper for each of two records and sets a flag bit in each. It finishes by calling further helpers and ends in an endless loop.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0958
name: wait_for_helper_then_finish
description: Runs timed delay loops, clears global words, and polls a helper until its return value is non-negative. It then calls helpers depending on flag bits in a global word, sets that word to 65535, and returns.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:099A
name: copy_region_if_flagged
description: Clears bit seven of a global flag byte, calls several helpers, and when bit two of the saved flag byte is set it copies a region in ten-longword strides, repeating seventy-six times. The source and destination addresses are computed identically, so each copy writes values back to where they were read.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:09A8
name: copy_region_from_flag
description: Clears bit seven of a flag byte in a record, calls helpers for the saved flag's low bits, and when bit two is set repeats a ten-longword-stride copy seventy-six times. The source and destination addresses are computed identically, so the copy is in place.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:09FE
name: copy_eight_blocks_in_place
description: Copies eight groups of ten longwords starting at a global base plus the input offset. The source and destination addresses are computed identically, so each value is written back to where it was read.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0A14
name: copy_blocks_by_count
description: Works out a block count from bits of a flag byte and an initial value, then copies blocks of ten longwords for that count. The source and destination addresses are computed identically, so the copy is in place.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0A84
name: copy_fixed_longword_blocks
description: Copies seventy-six blocks of sixteen longwords from one address to another, advancing both pointers by ten longwords per block. Each block is copied as a fixed set of indexed longwords.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0ACC
name: update_level_and_countdown_bytes
description: Returns early when a helper reports a flag and a table bit are both set. Otherwise it advances a counter byte, adds a value derived from another byte to a level byte clamped to a maximum, and when a countdown byte is zero calls a helper; it then updates the countdown byte from a flag byte and returns a packed result.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0AFC
name: update_level_countdown_alt
description: Performs the same level and countdown byte update as its counterpart, without the early exit or the returned value.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0B78
name: clamp_byte_field
description: Reads a byte at offset seven of a record, adds a value derived from a register and a constant, and clamps the result to the byte at offset eight. It writes the clamped byte back to offset seven.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0B90
name: decrement_global_and_iterate
description: Loops sixteen times, calling a helper with a decreasing short value and an increasing pointer value. It then decrements a global variable, calls two other routines, and clamps the global variable to zero if it is negative.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0BD6
name: call_five_helper_routines
description: The decompiler timed out, so only the listed facts are available. They show 51 instructions that call five other routines and are reached from one caller through an address reference; the purpose cannot be determined from this evidence.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0C74
name: call_seven_helper_routines
description: The decompiler timed out, so only the listed facts are available. They show 36 instructions that call seven other routines and are reached from two callers; the purpose cannot be determined from this evidence.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0CFC
name: decrement_global_and_table
description: Decrements a global counter, and when it goes negative resets it to seven and walks sixteen 32-byte records. For each record it decrements the byte at offset 21 and clears that byte when it reaches zero.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0D28
name: compact_entry_table_and_decrement
description: Walks a table of four-byte entries whose count is held in a global word. Entries whose longword is all ones are removed by shifting the following entries up and terminating the table with two 65535 words, while other entries have their flag bytes checked and decremented in a secondary table. It returns when the count is negative.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0D8C
name: compact_entry_table_from_registers
description: Repeats the table compaction and per-entry counter decrement of its counterpart, working from pointer and count values held in registers. It stops when the count reaches minus one or when an entry has no active counters.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0DA2
name: process_entry_counters_loop
description: Walks a list of four-byte entry records, clearing bit seven of a flag and resetting a byte in the secondary table for entries whose counters reach zero. Entries that are removed have the later records shifted up over them.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0DB8
name: shift_entries_and_update_flags
description: Walks a table of four-byte entries, decrementing a per-entry counter and shifting later entries up when an entry is removed. When an entry is removed it sets a flag byte and rewrites a packed nibble pair in the secondary table, then writes the 65535 terminator words.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0E0C
name: decrement_indexed_counters_loop
description: Walks a table of four-byte entries whose count sits just before the table. For each entry it decrements a byte in the global area addressed by the entry's offset by four; when that byte was below four it calls a helper, and otherwise, for entries with a set flag and sign bit, it calls another helper with a value from the table.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0E28
name: decrement_indexed_counters_alt
description: Performs the same walk over the four-byte entry table as its counterpart, decrementing the indexed bytes by four and calling helpers on the same conditions, using a base register and count held in registers.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0E4E
name: decrement_indexed_counters_with_helper
description: Calls a helper, then walks the same four-byte entry table, decrementing a counter byte per entry and calling helpers for entries that reach a threshold, until the end of the table.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0E52
name: conditional_helper_calls_by_flag
description: Tests bit one of a byte in a record at a register-held offset and calls a helper with that byte shifted right by two. When the bit is set it makes further helper calls depending on the sign of the returned value, the value of a threshold of 16, and a flag in the record.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0E88
name: check_and_combine_flag
description: Calls one helper, then calls two more helpers when a short register value is negative. It returns a 64-bit value built from a short taken from the stack and the input argument.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0EAA
name: remove_entry_and_shrink_count
description: Clears the low three bits of a 16-bit field at a computed offset, then removes one entry from an array of longwords by shifting the later entries down one place and reducing the stored byte count by four.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0EC4
name: copy_words_and_decrement_short
description: Copies a number of 32-bit words from a source pointer to a destination pointer, counting down until the counter reaches minus one. It then decrements a 16-bit value located two bytes before the destination base by four.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0ED0
name: update_entry_frame_state
description: Runs a per-frame update that, when a global word is zero, sets a timer value and calls six helpers, then toggles a bit through a further helper. It then removes entries whose counter low bits have reached a set pattern, calls helpers for sixteen indexed slots, and decrements counter bytes in two tables, calling helpers for those that go negative.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0F4A
name: update_entry_frame_state_tail
description: Performs the entry removal, indexed slot helper calls and counter decrements of the second half of its sibling routine, without the timer setup that begins that routine.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0F6A
name: compact_entries_and_update_frame
description: Copies four-byte table entries forward over removed ones, decrementing the stored count as it goes. It then performs the same indexed slot helper calls and counter decrements as its siblings and returns once the table is exhausted.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:0FF8
name: decrement_two_counter_tables
description: Decrements the positive entries of two four-entry signed byte tables held in a record. When an entry in the first table goes below zero it calls a helper, and if any entry did so it calls a helper once more; entries of the second table call a helper on the same condition. It returns nothing.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1058
name: stub_return_immediately
description: Returns immediately and does nothing. It is reached through an address reference from two callers.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:105E
name: update_slot_timer_and_flags
description: Returns early unless a global byte matches a byte of the record. Otherwise it counts down a low-nibble timer, and when the timer expires it reloads it and calls helpers with constant values chosen by flag bits in the record, clearing each flag whose helper reports zero.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1070
name: update_slot_timer_alt
description: Updates a record field from a helper's result, then performs the same timer countdown and flag-driven helper calls as its neighbouring routine for the slot.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:10AE
name: update_slot_timer_tail
description: Sets a record's low-nibble timer from an input value, then for each flag bit in the record calls helpers with constant values and clears any flag whose helper reports zero. It returns the value from the last helper call.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1130
name: dispatch_slot_helpers_on_flags
description: Returns early when the record byte at the index is negative. Otherwise it reads a second record byte, calls several helpers to compute a table position, and when a byte at that position has its high bit clear it calls further helpers using values from the record, returning the result of the last call.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1182
name: copy_slot_bytes_or_helper
description: Computes a value from the table address and index flag. When that value is negative it calls helpers and copies four bytes through helper calls, otherwise it calls one helper and returns, and it returns nothing.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:119A
name: copy_slot_bytes_alt
description: Performs the same conditional copy as its neighbouring routine: when a computed table value is negative it calls helpers and copies four bytes, and otherwise it calls one helper and returns.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:11A6
name: update_slot_state_with_checks
description: Evaluates a record's state byte and mask bits against an input word, then updates the slot through helper calls under the conditions the checks establish. It returns a value derived from the last helper result.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:136A
name: lookup_table_byte_and_update
description: Reads a byte from a table at an index computed from the input and a global value. When that byte is zero or all ones it calls a helper and updates the result from it; otherwise it takes a second helper path and returns the combined value.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:13A4
name: evaluate_slot_action_state
description: Evaluates a slot's state from an input value, record fields and table bits, calling nine helpers to update timers, flags and table entries. It returns the resulting state value.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:148A
name: link_slot_in_lookup_table
description: Either swaps a pair of table flag bits between two positions and toggles a record flag, or stores two record bytes and calls helpers. When a matching entry is found in a fixed lookup table it calls helpers with the value associated with that entry.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:14BA
name: clear_set_toggle_bits
description: Clears the high bit of one table byte, sets the high bit of another, and toggles bit one of a record byte. It returns nothing.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:14DE
name: index_byte_from_table
description: Reads a byte from a record at an offset and returns the global table entry selected by its high nibble and its low two bits.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:14F8
name: update_record_low_bits
description: Calls helpers and, when a global flag condition holds, updates the low two bits of a record byte at offset two by adding a helper result. Otherwise it follows a second helper path, and it returns the updated byte.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1530
name: select_slot_action_by_type
description: Returns early when a record byte equals the letter d. For action codes within a range it dispatches on the type code, copying two record bytes into the slot and calling helpers, and it returns the helper result.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1592
name: register_slot_in_lookup_table
description: Possibly registers the record in a four-entry lookup table: when the record's flag is negative it allocates a new table index, writes a sentinel and an offset there, and clears a flag. Otherwise it updates the low two bits of a record byte from a helper result.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:15F2
name: clear_flag_and_write_byte
description: Writes a byte derived from a pointer offset into memory addressed by a register, sets the byte at the pointer to 255, calls a helper, and clears the high bit of the byte at the offset the helper returns.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:161E
name: update_slot_timer_state
description: Calls helpers for a record whose status byte is negative. When a state field equals one it resets that field and updates a table entry, and it returns the final helper value.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1638
name: update_slot_state_and_table
description: Calls helpers and, when the record's state field equals one, sets it to one and reads two record bytes. It then calls a helper and conditionally calls more helpers depending on the sign of a table byte.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:165E
name: update_slot_stats_from_table
description: Calls helpers and, when a record state field equals one, reads two table-indexed values and a record field. It computes a combined value clamped against a global and updates the record fields from it.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:16E6
name: reset_or_refresh_slot_entries
description: If the record byte is negative, sets a field to seven, sets a global word to minus one, and calls two helpers. Otherwise it calls a helper for each of two table entries whose flag is non-negative.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1720
name: set_byte_and_clear_global
description: Writes the value seven to the byte at offset five of the record, sets a global word to minus one, and calls two helpers in turn.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1752
name: clear_table_bit_for_slot
description: Calls helpers and, when a record flag byte is negative, clears a single bit in a table byte selected by a helper result. It then resets a global counter and calls further helpers.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:178C
name: update_slot_bit_state
description: Calls helpers and updates bit fields of a record based on table lookups, returning a combined value built from the helper results.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1814
name: update_slot_bit_state_alt
description: Performs a similar table-driven bit update of a record through helper calls as its neighbouring routine, returning a combined value from the helper results.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1840
name: set_global_from_table_flag
description: Reads a flag byte from a table at an index. When its high bit is set it sets a global to minus one and calls a helper chosen by the low bits; otherwise it sets the global to zero and calls helpers, returning the result.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1858
name: update_low_bits_from_helper
description: Calls a helper and updates the low two bits of a record byte at offset two by adding the helper result to it, keeping the high nibble unchanged.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:186E
name: store_combined_flag_bits
description: Stores the bitwise OR of two byte values into a record byte at offset two plus an index, and returns nothing.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1876
name: update_slot_bit_pair_flags
description: Tests a pair of flag bits in a table byte selected by a record's low two bits. When they are not both set it calls a helper and then clears a table bit or updates the record's low bits; otherwise it clears the matching bit in the table and returns.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:18A2
name: update_slot_bit_flags_alt
description: Clears a table bit selected by the record's low bits when a pair of table flags matches, returning early. Otherwise it updates the record's low two bits from a helper result.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:18E8
name: copy_slot_record_to_table
description: When the target index differs from the stored one, either copies four longwords of the record into a fixed table and calls helpers, or toggles bit one of the record byte and continues. It then updates the record's low two bits and calls further helpers.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1926
name: copy_slot_record_when_flagged
description: Copies four longwords into a fixed table and calls helpers when a flag byte from a helper result is negative. Otherwise it toggles bit one of the record byte and calls helpers depending on the record's type code.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:193E
name: copy_four_longwords_to_table
description: Copies four longwords from a source pointer into a fixed table, calls a helper, stores a byte from memory into a global variable, and then calls a second helper.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1974
name: walk_slot_chain_and_store
description: Loops over a chain of slot records, calling helpers and comparing each record's index with an input index. When the indices match it toggles bit one of the record byte, and when the chain ends it stores a packed pair of bytes into the record.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1990
name: walk_slot_chain_until_match
description: Repeatedly compares a record's index with an input index, toggling a record bit when they match and calling helpers for records of a particular type code, until the chain ends or a match is found.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:199C
name: walk_slot_chain_alt
description: Walks the same record chain as its neighbouring routines, calling helpers for records of a specific type code and storing a packed pair of bytes into the record when the walk finds no further matches.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:19BE
name: scan_slot_chain_for_match
description: Walks records while the input index matches, toggling a record bit or calling helpers for records of a specific type code, and stores a packed pair of bytes when the walk ends.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:19F8
name: dispatch_slot_by_type_range
description: For records whose type code lies outside the range 136 to 138, sets a global from a record field and calls helpers before returning. For records inside the range it copies four longwords into a fixed table and calls helpers depending on flag bits.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1A5C
name: set_flag_and_record_entry
description: Sets the flag bit with value 32 in a byte addressed from an index and a base, increments a global entry counter, and stores the index and a shifted value of the second input into the table entry at the previous counter position. It returns nothing.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1A80
name: update_slot_table_entries
description: Calls six helpers while updating slot table state from several register inputs, and returns a combined value built from the results.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1AD4
name: accumulate_and_fill_table
description: Sets a global word to minus one, sums the results of repeated helper calls into a 16-bit total clamped to 253, and writes that total into four consecutive bytes at a fixed offset.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1B16
name: update_counter_from_helpers
description: Calls five helpers and updates a record's counter or status byte from their results, with the branch taken depending on the input values.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1B42
name: update_record_counters_by_flag
description: When the carry flag from a helper is set, handles negative results by scanning four slots and calling helpers for slots whose top bits are clear. For small results it updates a record counter from a global value and calls helpers.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1B6E
name: clamp_byte_and_update_counter
description: Clears the byte at offset 17 of a record, calls a helper, then subtracts the global byte from the record's byte at offset 9, flooring at zero. It adds the byte at offset 21 to the global byte, clamps the sum to 100 and stores it at offset 21.

key: bloodwych (1989)(imageworks)[cr qtx][h theft starters]/Bloodwych (1989)(ImageWorks)[cr QTX][h Theft Starters].adf:c/bloodwych:0:1B9E
name: check_flag_bytes_loop
description: Calls a helper, then tests four record bytes for having all of their top three bits clear. For each byte that does, it calls two helpers, and it calls two more helpers at the end.
